which_table.answer: The building code's table (2018 IBC Chapter 29, Table 2902.1). Settled by a signed Building Division policy and by Boise's own amendment to IBC Section 101.4.3. The plumbing code's Table 422.1 is not used for counts in Boise.
which_table.policy_quote: The number of required plumbing fixtures in a building or space shall be determined in accordance with the applicable requirements in Chapter 29 of the currently adopted edition of the International Building Code. ... Plumbing fixtures shall be installed per the applicable requirements of the currently adopted edition of the Idaho State Plumbing Code (Uniform Plumbing Code). ... Intent: The purpose of this policy is to clarify the IBC code is to be used for determining the required number of plumbing fixtures within a building or space and for applying accessibility requirements. The UPC code is to be used for plumbing fixture installation requirements. This current policy updates and replaces an existing policy on the subject from 3/12/10.
which_table.policy: City of Boise Planning and Development Services, Building Division Policy: Plumbing Fixtures Determination Policy, signed by Building Official Jason Blais, effective 2/22/24
which_table.code_quote: 101.4.3 Plumbing. The provisions of the plumbing code as adopted and amended by Boise City shall apply to the installation, alteration, repair, and replacement of plumbing systems, including equipment, appliances, fixtures, fittings, and appurtenances, where connected to a water or sewage system, and all aspects of medical gas systems. The number of required plumbing fixtures shall be determined by using IBC Table 2902.1 and pursuant to the International Plumbing Code Sections as referenced in the Table 2902.1.
which_table.code_section: Boise City Code 9-1A-4, IBC Building Code Amendment, Section 101.4.3, Applicable Plumbing Code
which_table.code_note: Read in the draft of 9/9/20 (mark-up resolved). The sentence on Table 2902.1 already carried the history note Ord. 44-17, 12-19-2017, eff. 1-1-2018; the draft changed only 'as per' to 'pursuant to'.

footnotes.text: Boise amends only footnotes e and f of Table 2902.1, with the same wording as the state rule: no service sink in business (not restaurant) and mercantile occupancies of 30 or fewer, no drinking fountain at 30 or fewer. Toilet ratios are unchanged.
footnotes.quote: Delete footnote (e) under Table 2902.1 Minimum Number of Required Plumbing Fixtures, and replace with the following: e. For business occupancies, excluding restaurants, and mercantile occupancies with an occupant load of thirty (30) or fewer, service sinks shall not be required. ... f. Drinking fountains are not required for an occupant load of thirty (30) or fewer.

urinals.text: Boise's 9-1A-4 keeps the International Plumbing Code sections that Table 2902.1 points to, so the table's urinal reference (IPC Section 424.2) applies in Boise even though Idaho has not adopted the IPC. 2018 IPC 424.2 lets urinals replace up to 67 percent of the required water closets in assembly and educational occupancies and up to 50 percent in other occupancies, per toilet room. No urinals are required.
urinals.quote: In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets in all other occupancies.
urinals.note: IPC 2018 Section 424.2 read on UpCodes in Utah's copy of the 2018 IPC (secondary, another state's adoption); the ICC site blocks automated access. Browser check before launch.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Boise job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material for Boise's dry climate and see the rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Boise offices, schools, clinics and manufacturing plants, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Boise sets the number of toilets by how many people use the building, using the table in Idaho's building rules. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Boise's list of work that needs no permit covers painting, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work, and movable partitions up to 5 feet 9 inches high. It doesn't name toilet partitions, which are fixed in place. The city handles interior alterations to commercial spaces as tenant improvement permits. Ask the Boise Building Division whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.stalls_intro: Boise counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. Half are counted as men and half as women, and every toilet used by staff or the public needs its own stall with a door. Idaho has two tables for the count, one in its building rules and one in its plumbing rules. Boise's Building Division has a written policy that the building rules decide the number, and the city's own building code says the same. That table gives one number of toilets for each sex and does not require urinals, so the table below shows the men's side as stalls.
page.stalls_after: Urinals are optional in Boise. The city's building code lets urinals replace up to two thirds of the men's toilets in a restaurant or school restroom and up to half in other buildings, so confirm the split with Boise plan review. These are minimums for the whole building, and at least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20. Your architect or the Boise Building Division sets the final number.
page.install_rule: Boise does not license contractors itself. The installer's Idaho contractor registration number, or a statement that the installer is exempt, goes on the city permit application, which is filed with Planning and Development Services. Idaho requires contractors to register with the state for jobs over $2,000. Publicly funded jobs of $50,000 or more, such as school projects, need a separate Public Works Contractor license. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor on a job over $2,000 needs an Idaho contractor registration.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Idaho has no wage law for public construction and bars the state, cities and school districts from setting wage rates on their projects, so a required wage applies only on federally funded work. For a carpenter on building work in Ada County that federal rate is $22.49 an hour plus $3.61 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 6% in Boise. That is the state rate: Boise and Ada County add no sales tax of their own.
page.buyers_extra: - **State offices, colleges and hospitals:** phenolic or stainless steel for busy public restrooms, with accessible stalls in every room.

Checked 2026-11-24.

- Which table sets toilet counts in Boise: City of Boise Building Division, [Plumbing Fixtures Determination Policy, effective February 22, 2024](https://www.cityofboise.org/media/3492/plumbing_fixtures_determination_policy_signed_2-22-24.pdf), from the division's [policies page](https://www.cityofboise.org/departments/planning-and-development-services/building/policies/); and Boise City Code Section 9-1A-4 (amendment to International Building Code Section 101.4.3), read in the city's [draft of Title 9, Chapter 1A, Building Code, dated September 9, 2020](https://www.cityofboise.org/media/10802/title-9-chapter-1a-2018-ibc-ordinance-draft-9-9-20.pdf). The codified chapter is in the [Boise City Code library](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/boise_id/latest/boise/0-0-0-36666), which could not be opened. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Urinals in place of toilets: 2018 International Plumbing Code Section 424.2, which Table 2902.1 and Boise City Code Section 9-1A-4 point to, read on [UpCodes](https://up.codes/viewer/utah/ipc-2018/chapter/4/fixtures-faucets-and-fixture-fittings), a secondary copy. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Work exempt from a permit in Boise: Boise City Code Section 9-1A-14 (amendment to International Building Code Section 105.2), read in the same [draft of Title 9, Chapter 1A](https://www.cityofboise.org/media/10802/title-9-chapter-1a-2018-ibc-ordinance-draft-9-9-20.pdf); commercial interior alterations in [Minor Tenant Improvement (518)](https://www.cityofboise.org/departments/planning-and-development-services/building/building-permits/commercial-construction-500/518-minor-tenant-improvement/) and the [Minor Tenant Improvement Guide](https://www.cityofboise.org/media/3821/518-b-user-guide-handout_may-2024.pdf). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Contractor registration number on Boise permit applications: City of Boise, [Contractor Registration Declaration Form (302), June 2026](https://www.cityofboise.org/media/9128/302-contractor-declaration-form_june-2026.pdf). Checked 2026-11-24.

- No local sales tax in Boise: Idaho State Tax Commission, [City Sales Taxes](https://tax.idaho.gov/taxes/sales-use/sales-tax/local-sales-tax/city-sales-tax/), whose list of cities with local sales taxes does not include Boise. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Ada County carpenter rate on federally funded building work: [federal wage determination ID20260104, modification 2, May 18, 2026](https://sam.gov/wage-determination/ID20260104/2). Checked 2026-11-24.
